apparatus.basis: Editor restoration; ⲡⲁⲇⲁⲙⲁⲥ 'Adamas' (of Light) is the standard Manichaean warrior figure, completed at start of next line by ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'of Light.'
Editor restoration of relative-identifying formula ⲉⲧⲉ ... ⲡⲉ; the surviving ⲁϩ continues with the verb 'to be.'
Editor restoration; ⲡϣⲁⲙⲧ 'the three' is required by the immediately following 'wheels' (the Three Wheels of fire/wind/water of Manichaean cosmology).
Editor restoration; ⲁⲩϣⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ = 'they were disturbed/troubled' (= Sah. ϣⲧⲟⲣⲧⲣ̄), an attested Manichaean cosmic-disturbance verb.
Editor restoration; ⲛⲧⲁⲩ = 'they' (perfect/relative); fits subject-marker for the following lacuna.
Editor restoration; ⲍⲓⲁⲩⲉ = ϩⲓⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'roads, paths' fits the preceding ⲙⲁⲓⲧ 'paths' in line 13.
Editor restoration; the directional preposition + article completes the purpose-clause structure.
Editor restoration of ⲡⲧⲏⲩ 'the wind'; the standard Manichaean triad with ⲡⲙⲁⲩ 'water' and ⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire' (the three light-elements rising from the abortions at the Third Ambassador's revelation).
Editor restoration of formulaic chapter-opener ⲧⲧⲁⲁⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ 'Once again' (= ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ in glossary), as in lines 9 and (implicitly) 24.
Restoration of ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'all of them'; 2-character lacuna fits ⲧⲏ; standard direct object after ⲡⲉⲧⲑⲃⲓⲟ 'who humbles.'
Editor restoration; ⲃⲉⲟ̄ⲥⲉ 'depth, abyss' (Crum ⲃⲏⲏⲥⲉ); same word recurs at line 23 (ⲧⲃⲉⲟ̄ⲥⲉ).
Editor restoration of definite article preceding ⲧⲗⲁⲓⲟ̄ⲉ.
Editor restoration completing ⲫⲉⲣⲣⲟⲕⲁⲧⲟⲭⲟⲥ from previous line.
Editor restoration of plural article before ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲟⲥ 'helpers.'
Editor restoration; ⲛⲍⲣⲏϣⲉ 'the burdens' is the standard Manichaean term for the cosmic loads borne by the Pillar of Glory and Omophoroi (cf. accumulated vocab ⲭⲁⲩⲗⲉ 'bear up the ⲍⲣⲏϣⲉ').
Editor restoration completing ⲉⲓⲣⲏⲅⲟⲣⲟⲥ 'Egregoros' (Watcher) from previous line.
Editor restoration of perfect prefix; ⲁⲩⲃⲱⲧⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'they expelled' (the giants/sons of the Watchers from the earth).
Editor restoration; ⲉⲡⲉⲓⲇⲏ 'since, because' is the standard discourse-marker opening a causal clause.
Editor restoration of perfect prefix completing ⲁⲩⲭⲡⲟ 'they begot.'
Editor restoration; ⲉⲧⲁϩϣⲱⲡⲉ 'which arose,' relative perfect, parallels the same construction at line 24.
Editor restoration; ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛⲁⲇⲁⲙ 'the mind of Adam' is the standard Manichaean phrase for the awakening of Adam by Jesus.

notes.decision: Translated 'strife' throughout the page (lines 1, 23, 30) for this recurring noun denoting the cosmic battle. The opening 'a strife arose' parallels Manichaean cosmogonic-historical narrative; ⲕⲣⲁϩ is paired with ⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ-class semantics. Etymology uncertain — possibly Lyc form related to a martial root; flagged in proposed_terms.
Read as feminine possessive ⲧⲉϩ- + ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲟⲗⲏ 'her encampment,' parallel to masculine ⲡⲉϩ- in glossary. Antecedent presumably continues from previous page — likely Hyle/Matter or the world.

Translated 'the chosen one' per accumulated vocabulary, though here the referent appears to be the encampment (= the earth/world?) rather than Zarathustra. The sense 'the elect (place)' may be intended.

Compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix) + ⲡⲁⲓⲥ. Translated 'place of battle' since the figure named is Adamas of Light, the cosmic warrior who battles the dark powers. ⲡⲁⲓⲥ here likely denotes combat/striking/contest. Etymology of ⲡⲁⲓⲥ uncertain; flagged in proposed_terms.
Translated 'the Great Counsel' per accumulated vocabulary entry. Here identified with the Great King of Glory and described as having authority over the three wheels (fire/wind/water).
Translated 'they sank' — Lycopolitan form likely from ⲗⲱⲕϩ̄ 'cast, throw, immerse.' Intransitive sense fits: the abortions are submerged/stuck in the three earths until the Ambassador's revelation.

Translated 'were laid open' — qualitative/perfect of an unidentified verb related to opening or stretching paths. Context (after the Ambassador reveals his image) requires path-opening semantics. Confidence low; flagged in proposed_terms.
Parsed as ⲧ-ⲟⲩ-ⲟⲓⲛ-ⲉⲓ 'their coming' (action-noun ⲟⲓⲛ- on ⲉⲓ 'come'), parallel to the formation ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'the dissolution' in vocab.
Singular 'the Omophoros' — distinct from plural ⲛⲱⲙⲟⲫⲟⲣⲟⲥ in vocab. Refers here to the chief Atlas-figure, also called Pillar of Glory.
Translated 'boundaries' tentatively from ⲧⲱϣ 'boundary, limit.' Lyc reflex with ⲱⲟ̄ⲥ for ⲱϣ.

Greek ἐγρήγοροι 'Watchers' — the fallen Watchers of 1 Enoch tradition, integrated into Manichaean cosmology as a class of fallen powers bound by the four angels in the prison of darkness. Their sons (the giants) are then expelled from the earth (line 28).
Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'prison.' The 'prison of the dark ones' = the eschatological-cosmic prison of the fallen Watchers.
'their sons' = the giants, sons of the Watchers and human women per 1 Enoch — expelled from the earth in the standard reception of the myth.
Translated 'he cast them downward' — ⲧⲁⲟ̄ⲥⲟⲩ likely from ⲧⲁⲩⲉ/ⲧⲁⲟⲩⲟ 'put forth, cast' with 3pl object suffix. Context: Jesus casting down the abortions at his revelation.
